puzzle1.title: Rescue the Helix
puzzle1.description: This 42-residue peptide should fold into a single continuous α-helix, but six helix-breaking residues (Pro and Gly) have been inserted at structurally bad positions. Mutate residues to restore the helix. Score = Cα RMSD to the target structure (lower is better).
puzzle1.hint: Helix-breaking residues are P and G. Helix-favoring are A, E, K, L, M.

puzzle2.title: Rebuild the Bundle
puzzle2.description: HP35 (villin headpiece) is a classic 36-residue 3-helix bundle. Five mutations have damaged its core. WARNING: protein folding is cooperative — fixing one mutation in isolation may not improve the score (or may briefly make it worse). The structure 'snaps' into place once enough breakers are reverted. Score = Cα RMSD to wild-type HP35.
puzzle2.hint: Helices need contiguous helix-favoring residues. Look for Pro and Gly in helical regions.

puzzle3.title: Cage the Trp
puzzle3.description: Trp-cage (PDB 1L2Y) is the smallest fast-folding miniprotein known, with a single tryptophan locked inside a polyproline cage. Three mutations have killed the hydrophobic core. Restore the cage.
puzzle3.hint: The tryptophan at position 6 (W) sits in the centre of the cage. The prolines at 12 and 19 hold the polyproline loop together.

puzzle4.title: Crack the Core
puzzle4.description: HP35 (villin headpiece) again — but this time the breakers killed the hydrophobic core, not the helices. Phe and Trp swapped for charged residues. Restore the core so the bundle can pack.
puzzle4.hint: Charged residues (D, E, K) don't belong in a hydrophobic core. Trp (W) and Phe (F) are big aromatics that hold the core together. Helix-breaking Pro and Gly also need to go.

puzzle5.title: Three-helix Bundle
puzzle5.description: A 56-residue 3-helix bundle DNA-binding motif (Engrailed homeodomain family). Five mutations have wrecked the inter-helix packing — hydrophobic core residues swapped for polar/charged ones. Restore the packing so the three helices can pack together.
puzzle5.hint: Hydrophobic cores need hydrophobic residues. F (Phe), Y (Tyr), W (Trp), I (Ile), L (Leu), V (Val) are the usual core residues. Charged residues (D, E, K, R) don't belong in the centre.

puzzle6.title: Hairpin Lost
puzzle6.description: The GB1 β-hairpin (PDB 2GB1 residues 41-56) is one of the smallest, fastest-folding β-sheet motifs known. Five core residues have been swapped for charge or helix-breakers and the hairpin has unwound. Restore the strand pairing.
puzzle6.hint: β-strands love branched/aromatic residues: V, I, T, W, Y, F. Charged residues (K, D, E) and the helix-breaker Pro don't pair into sheets. The DDA at positions 6-8 is the turn — leave it alone.

puzzle7.title: Zipper Down
puzzle7.description: GCN4-p1 leucine zipper (yeast transcription factor coiled-coil). As a single chain ESMFold predicts a clean α-helix held together by buried Leucines at every 7th position. Six Leucines (4 core + 2 surface) have been swapped — some for the helix-breaker Pro, some for charged Glu — and the helix has unwound.
puzzle7.hint: Coiled-coils pack their hydrophobic core every 7th residue (heptad-d). Buried Leucines were swapped for charged Glu or for the helix-breaker Pro. Find the L→E and L→P swaps and revert.
